claims.head: Don’t count on Vasilevskiy to stand on his head again
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Vasilevskiy has been a wall against the Flyers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Vasilevskiy.
claims.nums: 7 starts against Philadelphia: .944 save percentage · .910 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Vasilevskiy’s record against the Flyers.
claims.call: If Vasilevskiy starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .910 than to his .944 against the Flyers.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 7 against Philadelphia, 4,532 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: Expect the Lightning to fire from everywhere
claims.call: The Lightning take at least their usual 60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Philadelphia has been giving up shots all season, and the Lightning rarely pass one up.
claims.nums: Tampa Bay 6th for shot volume (60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Philadelphia 28th for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Lightning shoot a lot, and the Flyers give up plenty.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season

check.measure: 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 3 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 61%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
